theory.name: Generic Provenance Workflow
theory.summary: A neutral formal example showing how non-executable theory packages declare exact operator contracts.
theory.motivation: Demonstrate portable provenance and review semantics without publishing or depending on any private research program.

objects.name: Record
objects.definition: A versioned item with a stable identifier, content hash, and addressable ancestry.

objects.name: Claim
objects.definition: A bounded proposition with status, evidence references, and an immutable version identity.

objects.name: Review result
objects.definition: A decision record naming the reviewed claim, reviewer class, checks, and disposition.

operators.name: attach_source
operators.semantics: Create a new claim version whose evidence set includes the supplied record while preserving prior ancestry.

preconditions: The claim and record have stable identifiers and content hashes.
The record is not already attached to the current claim version.

predicates.statement: Every prior ancestor of the input claim remains reachable from the output claim version.
The supplied record appears exactly once in the output evidence set.

failure_conditions.condition: Either input lacks a stable identifier or content hash.
The source record is already attached.
Any prior claim ancestry becomes unreachable.

reversibility.condition: A later superseding claim version may remove the active attachment only while preserving a tombstone and the prior version.

contract.first_falsifier: An admissible attachment that produces a new claim version from which a prior ancestor or the supplied record cannot be addressed.

operators.name: review_claim
operators.semantics: Evaluate a claim against a declared evidence record and emit a bounded review disposition without mutating the claim.

parameters.name: Reviewer class
parameters.constraints: Must be one of the package-authorized reviewer classes.

preconditions: The claim and evidence record are addressable.
The reviewer class is authorized for this review type.

predicates.statement: The review result names exact claim and evidence identities.
The disposition states what was checked and prohibits unsupported promotion.

failure_conditions.condition: The reviewer class is not authorized.
The evidence record cannot be resolved.
The review attempts to promote beyond the declared checks.

reversibility.condition: A review result is append-only; later reviews may supersede but do not erase it.

contract.first_falsifier: A valid review result that cannot identify its claim, evidence, reviewer class, checks, or bounded disposition.

assumptions.text: Every object has a stable identifier and deterministic content hash.
Version history is append-only; supersession does not erase prior versions.

invariants.text: All prior claim ancestry remains addressable after a source attachment.
Every review result remains attached to the exact claim, evidence, checks, and disposition that produced it.

allowed: the package defines a portable formal provenance workflow
an implementation may be built against the declared contracts
prohibited: the example is an empirical theory
a valid manifest proves an implementation correct
a review result establishes truth beyond its declared checks

evidence.notes: This neutral package is a formal governance example and has no empirical truth claim.
